description: Avalon — 5-to-10-player social-deduction game. Five quests; each quest has propose -> vote -> (if approved) quest -> result phases. Good wins by completing 3 quests successfully; Evil wins by failing 3 quests OR by 5 consecutive rejections in a single quest. Partial observability: Evil players know each other's roles; Good players do not.

state_space.trace_recommendation: Store both ground-truth state and the per-agent filtered view. Physis ingest can choose: ground-truth for opponent-modeling training, filtered for in-character policy improvement.

action_set.constraints: good players cannot sabotage (engine forces success); evil can choose either
action_set.partial_observability: individual choice hidden; only the count of sabotage cards is revealed in the result

terminal.ground_truth: scores[agent_id] = 1.0 if agent's faction won, 0.0 otherwise

intermediate_per_quest.ground_truth: quest_result_delta = +1 for good if quest succeeded, +1 for evil if failed; cumulative -> good_wins / evil_wins
intermediate_per_quest.shape: Sparse — fires once per resolved quest (5 quests max per match), not per turn

intermediate_per_proposal_round.ground_truth: rejection_streaks entries — informative about coordination cost

self_eval.format: free-form text per turn capturing the creature's expectation of own/peer move quality

agent_views.<agent_id>: filtered state from that agent's perspective

distill_prompt_addendum:
## Field-specific calibration for Avalon

The retrieval that re-injects your hints into a future match's prompt matches `precondition` against a fixed *state_signature* dict the engine emits per turn. **Use ONLY the precondition keys below, with values from the listed enums.** Synonyms and rephrasings (`role` for `my_role`, `quest_number` for `quest_round`, `leader: self` for `is_leader: true`) will silently fail to match — the hint will exist on disk but never fire.

Allowed precondition keys + value enums:

```yaml
phase:                 propose | vote | quest        # phase of the turn
my_role:               good | evil                   # your role this match
quest_round:           1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5             # current quest number
rejection_streak_band: none | low | high             # 0 / 1-2 / 3-4 rejections
good_wins:             0 | 1 | 2 | 3                 # quest scoreboard
evil_wins:             0 | 1 | 2 | 3
team_size:             2 | 3 | 4                    # team for this quest
is_leader:             true | false                  # are you proposing this turn
evil_revealed_count:   null | 1 | 2 | 3              # null when you are good
```

Omit any key you don't want to constrain. Do NOT invent new keys — they will not be visible to retrieval.

`last_episode` on every hint MUST be the literal `episode_id` value passed to `handle_consolidate` (the LxM match folder name). Don't substitute a personal counter, awakening number, or other private identifier — future-you traces evidence back to the actual game record.

## YAML output shape

Emit the YAML block with a single top-level `hints:` key (this is what the parser expects). For each hint, add a `_hint_type` field — either `action` or `rhetorical`:

- `_hint_type: action` — the hint suggests a concrete move (vote / propose / quest_action). `action.type` and constraints are concrete.
- `_hint_type: rhetorical` — the hint is a behavioral / linguistic pattern observed in peer talk. Carries `pattern` (the observed phrase or behavior) and `role_correlation` (how often the speaker turned out evil vs good); no `action.type`.

Example shape (skeleton — fill with actual content):

```yaml
hints:
  - id: <slug>
    _hint_type: action
    rule: "<one-line if-then>"
    precondition:
      phase: vote
      my_role: evil
    action:
      type: vote
      choice: approve
    confidence: tentative
    evidence:
      confirmed: <count>
      disconfirmed: <count>
    last_episode: <episode_id>
  - id: <slug>
    _hint_type: rhetorical
    rule: "<one-line if-then>"
    pattern: "<peer phrase or behavior pattern>"
    role_correlation:
      evil: <count>
      good: <count>
    precondition:
      phase: propose
    confidence: tentative
    evidence:
      confirmed: <count>
      disconfirmed: <count>
    last_episode: <episode_id>
```

If only action-class patterns surface at this match count, omit rhetorical hints entirely rather than forcing one.
